title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 34
paragraphs: To this headland the men assigned to the job were now building their bridges, starting from Abydos — the Phoenicians constructing one with ropes of white flax, the Egyptians the other with papyrus rope. From Abydos to the opposite shore is a distance of seven stades. When the strait had been bridged, a great storm came on and shattered the whole work, breaking it up. When Xerxes heard of it, he was beside himself with rage, and ordered the Hellespont scourged with three hundred lashes and a pair of fetters lowered into the sea. I have heard, moreover, that he sent branding-irons too, to brand the Hellespont. However that may be, he commanded his men, as they were lashing, to utter these barbarous and presumptuous words: “Bitter water, your master lays this penalty upon you, because you wronged him, having suffered no wrong from him. And Xerxes the king will cross you, whether you like it or not; it is with right, it seems, that no man sacrifices to you, since you are a treacherous and briny stream.” So he ordered the sea to be punished, and he also ordered the heads cut off of those in charge of bridging the Hellespont.
